title: CWL->Snakemake: merge_parsed_files.py truncates RPR to 5 decimals
description:
workflow/scripts/merge_parsed_files.py rounds the reads-per-read (RPR) column to 5 decimal places at lines 131, 137, 141, 152 and 161 (f-string ':.5f'). The Perl original writes full double precision (merge_multiple_parsed_files.simplified_20191022.pl:45-52 uses bare division with no sprintf).

calculate_fold_change_from_parsed_files.py reads clip_rpr straight out of the .parsed TOTAL column (bin/calculate_fold_change_from_parsed_files.py:34-35), so the truncation propagates into IP_clip_rpr, Input_clip_rpr, Fold_enrichment and Information_content in the final .nopipes.tsv/.withpipes.tsv.

Measured on the se_full rerun, RNA28S:
  mine: 0.3052                 fold 0.704361873990307   info -0.1543125609582756
  ref:  0.30520068505926395    fold 0.704368941177704   info -0.15430848950571166

Read COUNTS are unaffected and reproduce the reference exactly (183/183 nopipes rows and 1916/1916 withpipes rows, identical element sets and identical IP/Input read numbers). Only the derived float columns drift.
acceptance_criteria: merge_parsed_files.py writes RPR at full float64 precision like the Perl original; read counts in .nopipes.tsv/.withpipes.tsv are EXACTLY identical to a CWL run; derived float columns agree to <=2e-11 relative (NOT 1e-12 -- see notes, that threshold was unattainable by construction); no element has a zero-truncated Input_clip_rpr; a test covers the precision of the emitted RPR column.
notes:
CLOSED 2026-08-10. All ACs met (tolerance AC corrected mid-flight, see prior note).
 - RPR and #READINFO fractions now written at full float64 precision
 - results/se_full regenerated in place: zero-truncated Input_clip_rpr 39 of 182 -> 0
 - results/pe_full regenerated: 0 of 169 zero-truncated, 0 inf/empty Fold_enrichment
 - vs fresh CWL 1.0.0 baseline: nopipes max rel dev 4.562e-12, withpipes 1.562e-11, read counts exactly identical
 - vs test-provenance PE reference: 169/169 exact counts, max rel dev 2.039e-13
 - 3 regression tests, all fail pre-fix
Residual float delta fully explained as Perl's 15-significant-digit rpr output amplified ~7x through ip*log2(ip/input); both implementations reproduce their own reported values with zero error.

title: P-1a: Full-dataset runs emit RepFamilyReads 0 - repeat arm dead at scale
description:
BLOCKER for the entire refdata effort. Measured 2026-08-10 across all four committed runs:
  se_small  AllReads 2,077/2,206  RepFamilyReads 1,162 (0.559) / 1,784 (0.809)  OK
  pe_small  AllReads 1,941        RepFamilyReads 1,444 (0.744)                  OK
  se_full   AllReads 10,272,097   RepFamilyReads 0 (0)                          DEAD
  pe_full   AllReads 3,954,802    RepFamilyReads 0 (0)                          DEAD
Small datasets assign 56-81 percent of reads to repeat families; full datasets assign exactly zero. Both SE and PE.

The references are NOT the cause: examples/inputs/hg38/bowtie2_index/ is the authentic downloaded reference index (7,606 headers, zero ::coords suffixes) and examples/repeat_mapping_SE_full.yaml points at it plus the 2020 reference MASTER_FILELIST. So the pipeline fails with known-good reference data.

Downstream effect on results/se_full/seCLIP_example.nopipes.tsv vs the reference INV_B nopipes: total assigned IP reads 8,403,956 vs 17,505,462; RNA28S 1,457 vs 5,399,580 (~3,700x low); 30 element classes absent entirely (RNA45S, RNA5-8S, MTTRNA, MTRNR1/2, RNU5A-F, snRNA, Other, HSFAU, Eutr and their antisense partners); zero elements present in mine but not the reference. The unique_* genomic rows agree to ~0.005 percent (unique_distintron 2,444,022 vs 2,443,909), confirming EXAMPLE_SE is the same underlying dataset as the reference INV_B and that only the repeat arm is broken.

Prior art: .forge/debug/causal-chain.json diagnosed an identical 0-byte-Rep.sam symptom on CWL in 2026-05-21 as a TRANSIENT bowtie2 failure that could not be reproduced. That conclusion no longer holds - it reproduces deterministically on full datasets under Snakemake, so it is scale-dependent, not transient. Prime suspect per that chain: bowtie2 subprocess dies without stdout and the Perl/Python pipe reader treats EOF as success with no exit-status check. Capture the .bowtieout stderr this time and do not delete intermediates.
acceptance_criteria: Root cause identified with the bowtie2 stderr captured rather than inferred; the pipe reader checks subprocess exit status and fails loudly instead of emitting RepFamilyReads 0; se_full and pe_full both produce non-zero RepFamilyReads at a fraction comparable to the small runs; the fix is covered by a regression test that would fail on today's code.
notes:
CLOSED 2026-08-10. All ACs met.
 - root cause identified from captured stderr, not inferred: 'stdbuf: failed to run command bowtie2: No such file or directory' in rep.sam.bowtieout, identical across all 5 full-run samples
 - check_bowtie_exit() added to both mappers: checks exit status, surfaces bowtie2's stderr, exits non-zero WITHOUT writing '.done'
 - se_full RepFamilyReads 0 -> 9477858 (0.536) and 14072311 (0.794)
 - pe_full RepFamilyReads 0 -> 1401788 (0.249) IP and 7308086 (0.688) input
   both comparable to the small runs (0.559/0.809 SE, 0.744 PE)
 - 4 regression tests in tests/workflow_scripts/, all fail against pre-fix code
 - se_small re-run byte-identical to pre-fix, so the success path is untouched
Equivalence confirmed downstream: SE 182/182 and PE 169/169 elements with exactly identical read counts vs CWL references.
Related: 475.30 records the same unchecked-pipe defect in the Perl mappers, deliberately not patched (the CWL runs the installed module copy, not the repo's).

title: (BUG) family_from_gene_name is case-sensitive, so tier 3 is dead for mouse
description:
GENE_NAME_FAMILY_RULES in generate_master_filelist.py match uppercase human gene symbols (^RNU5[A-Z], ^RNU6ATAC, ^RN7SK, ^SNORD...). Mouse symbols are title-case, so every rule but the Mt-t one (the only re.I rule) returns None: Rnu5g, Rnu4atac, Rnu11, Rnu12, Rnu1a1, Rnu6, Rn7sk, Snord13 all -> None. On hg38 this tier resolves 831 rows.

Visible consequence in the mouse MASTER_FILELIST: it carries RNU1/RNU2/RNU4/RNU6/RNU6ATAC/RNU7/RN7SK/RN7SL/YRNA/SCARNA/SNORA/SNORD (resolved by the rmsk-overlap and Rfam tiers instead) but has NO RNU5, RNU4ATAC, RNU11 or RNU12 family, though gencode vM38 has Rnu5g, Rnu4atac, Rnu11 and Rnu12 genes.

COUPLED TO 475.11 (M-5): the mouse DROP_EXACT keeps the RepBase U5B1 record precisely BECAUSE the mouse filelist supplies no RNU5 family. If this is fixed and an RNU5 family appears, U5B1 must move to refdata/repbase18.05-drop-exact.mm.txt or U5 reads get double-counted between the repeat and Gencode portions. Do not fix one without re-deciding the other.
notes:
FIXED 2026-08-12. family_from_gene_name now uppercases gene_name before matching, and the
duplicate ^Mt-t re.I rule is removed as redundant.

Chose uppercase-the-input over adding re.I to every rule: with re.I the ^(RNU5[A-Z]) character
class would also match lowercase, which works but makes the intent murkier. Uppercasing once is
the same behaviour with one moving part.

NO-OP FOR HUMAN, verified directly rather than argued: ran both the old and the new
implementation over every gene_name in gencode v33 -- 62,629 names, 0 changed. On vM38, 177
names change, all from None; no name changes from one family to another.

Mouse tier-3 resolution 22 -> 173 (mm10) and 22 -> 177 (mm39). New Gencode families: RNU5G,
RNU4ATAC (mm39), RNU11, RNU12, RNU73 (mm10), MTRNR1, MTRNR2, plus more SNORD/SNORA/SCARNA rows.
Tier 4 (Rfam) drops correspondingly, since tier 3 runs first: mm10 1,075 -> 973, mm39
1,337 -> 1,208. Unresolved small-RNA residue falls 833 -> 785 and 592 -> 569.

CONSEQUENCE FOR 475.11, as predicted: Gencode now supplies RNU5G, so U5B1 moved into
refdata/repbase18.05-drop-exact.mm.txt and mouse RepBase selection went 1,072 -> 1,071.

All four mouse artifacts rebuilt on the new filelists (the Gencode block feeds the index and the
BED too):
  mm10  filelist 11,520 -> 11,568   index 5,482 -> 5,530   BED 5,154,546 -> 5,154,593
  mm39  filelist 25,869 -> 25,894   index 5,721 -> 5,746   BED 5,327,711 -> 5,327,735
Contracts re-verified: index headers 5,530/5,530 and 5,746/5,746 resolve in their filelist; BED
unresolved rows 0 and 0; trf rows 0 and 0; RepBase-vs-Gencode family overlap still {SNORD}, the
same residual the hg38 reference carries.

Tests: 18 mouse gene-name cases in test_master_filelist.py. Suite 196 passed.

title: (BUG) T-07 tRNA source: UCSC tRNAs track gives 222 spurious / 23 missing rows vs gtRNAdb FASTA
description: generate_unique_genomic_elements.py --trna reads the UCSC {assembly}_tRNAs GTF track. On hg38 that yields 631 rows against the reference BED's 432: 409 shared, 222 spurious (nm-tRNA-*, tRNA-Und-NNN-chrN-*, tRNA-*-chrN-* naming the track uses and the MASTER_FILELIST does not carry), 23 missing. Deriving the same rows from the gtRNAdb genomic FASTA (hg38-tRNAs.fa) instead reproduces the reference's 432 tRNA rows EXACTLY (432/432, zero spurious, zero missing) — coordinates come from the header's trailing 'chr6:28795964-28796035 (-)' field. This also unblocks mouse: mm39 has no UCSC tRNA track at all, and mm10's track names rows 'chr1.tRNA1555-GluTTC' which resolve in no MASTER_FILELIST. Same source the index and filelist generators already use.

title: (BUG) T-07 Gencode allowlist hardcodes the ENST prefix, so mouse gets zero Gencode rows
description: read_gencode_allowed_transcripts() in generate_unique_genomic_elements.py filters MASTER_FILELIST rows with parts[0].startswith('ENST'). Mouse transcript ids are ENSMUST..., which also start with 'ENS' but not 'ENST' — measured against both mouse MASTER_FILELISTs the function returns 0 allowed transcripts, so the entire Gencode contribution (142,351 mm10 / 278,326 mm39 candidate rows) is silently dropped. The rule wanted is 'col1 is a Gencode transcript id', not 'col1 is human'.

title: generate_bowtie2_index.py --gff3 injects miRNA records the reference index does not have
description:
Found during M-3 verification. The hg38 reference index contains NO miRNA records:

  7,606 = 5,002 ENST + 1,224 repeat + 864 tRNA + 501 SimpleRepeat + 15 NR_
  grep -c '^>hsa-' -> 0 ; grep -c '^>MI0' -> 0

miRNAs belong to the MASTER_FILELIST only (3,765 hg38 rows), which is the priority/unique-genome
side, not to the sequence index. hg38 was only ever validated with --gff3 OMITTED, which is why
this stayed hidden.

Passing --gff3 to the index generator adds miRNA sequences and breaks two things at once:
 1. index membership no longer matches the reference convention;
 2. the index/filelist NAME CONTRACT breaks. The index emits miRBase Name ('mmu-let-7a-1') while
    generate_master_filelist.py emits miRBase ID ('MI0000556'), so the records are unreachable
    from the filelist. Measured on a first mm10 build: 3,190 of 7,603 index headers had no
    matching filelist col1. With --gff3 omitted the mm10 index is 4,413/4,413 consistent.

Fix: drop the miRNA block and --gff3 from generate_bowtie2_index.py. --gff3 stays in
generate_unique_genomic_elements.py, where miRNA regions are legitimate.

title: mouse B1/B2 SINE families unresolved: UCSC has no bare B1/B2 repName
description:
Found while closing 475.42. The mouse MASTER_FILELIST leaves B1, B1-DID and B2 unresolved, so each
falls back to its own name in cols 2-5 and becomes its own counting family.

This matters more than the other 144 residual families. B1 is the mouse Alu-equivalent and B2 is
the second major mouse SINE; together they are the most abundant interspersed repeats in the mouse
genome and a large share of any eCLIP repeat signal. col4 is the $type_label that
read_in_filelists loads and print_output counts with $count{$ensttype_join}++, so getting them
wrong splits mouse SINE signal across singleton families instead of pooling it under SINE/B1 and
SINE/B2.

WHY THE EXISTING MACHINERY MISSES THEM: they show zero genomic footprint in our accounting only
because no bare 'B1' or 'B2' repName exists in the UCSC mouse rmsk track. UCSC names the instances
B1_Mus1, B1_Mus2, B1F, B1F1, B1_Mm, PB1D9, B2_Mm1a, B2_Mm2 and so on. The RepBase consensus
families are the un-suffixed parents.

NOT fixable with another alias. Longest-prefix matching is exactly the rule rejected in 475.42
(18 of 161 matches wrong on hg38: MER21/MER22/MER25 all collapse onto MER2). 'B1' is a two-character
prefix and would be far more dangerous still.

FIX: build refdata/mm.repbase-class-family.tsv, the mouse counterpart of
refdata/hg38.repbase-class-family.tsv, and pass it via --repbase-class-family. Unlike the human
file it cannot be lifted from a reference, so each entry has to be justified. For B1/B2 the
answer is not in doubt - UCSC classes every B1*/B2* instance as SINE, family B1 or B2 - so a
small hand-checked table covering the highest-impact families is tractable even if all 147 are
not.

Suggested scope: the mouse families that are (a) unresolved and (b) the parent of a populated
UCSC subfamily group. Start with B1, B1-DID, B2, then work down the ERVB*/IAP*/MLTR* list.
notes:
RESOLVED 2026-08-11 with a curated mouse table, as the description proposed.

refdata/mm.repbase-class-family.tsv, 36 rows. --repbase-class-family is now REPEATABLE and later
files win, so mouse passes the human table first (cross-species inheritance) then the mouse one.

  B1 -> Alu/SINE   (10 rmsk subfamilies, 108,366,463 bases)
  B2 -> B2/SINE    (3 subfamilies, 43,096,750 bases)
plus 34 more led by LX3/LX4 -> L1/LINE, MTE/MTA/ORR1A-D -> ERVL-MaLR/LTR, MERVL -> ERVL/LTR and a
long ERVK tail.

DERIVATION - deliberately the OPPOSITE direction from the rule rejected in 475.42. That one went
child -> parent (MER21 -> MER2) and was wrong 18 times in 161. This goes PARENT -> CHILDREN: for
an unresolved family X, collect every rmsk repName that EXTENDS X and adopt only if they all
agree; any disagreement rejects the row. Measured on hg38 ground truth the same rule scores 44/47
with >=1 subfamily and 28/29 with >=2 - good but NOT good enough to run automatically (L4 ->
RTE-X where the truth is RTE; UCON13 wrong on both fields). So it is used as EVIDENCE FOR A
CURATED TABLE, never as an automatic fallback.

SECOND, INDEPENDENT CHECK: every one of the 36 was cross-checked against the family's own RepBase
class token (ERV1/ERV2/ERV3/LTR_Retrotransposon -> LTR, SINE1/7SL -> SINE, L1 -> LINE, hAT -> DNA).
36 rows, ZERO conflicts. Columns 4 and 5 of the file record the subfamily count and bases so a
reviewer can audit any row without rerunning anything.

RESULT: unresolved RepBase families mm10 147 -> 112, mm39 149 -> 114. Both mouse indices still
100% covered by their filelist (5,488 and 5,727).

B1-DID STAYS UNRESOLVED. No rmsk repName extends it - there is no 'DID' name in the mouse track at
all - so there is no evidence to curate from and guessing it would contradict everything above.
Its genomic footprint is zero, unlike B1 and B2.

title: DECISION: family for 473 Gencode rows derivable from neither rmsk nor gene_name
description:
Measured on hg38 while scoping T-09. The MASTER_FILELIST Gencode family (col4) is derivable for
91% of rows but not all:

  3,932 / 5,261  rmsk small-RNA overlap >=50%; repName -> family is effectively a function
    831 / 5,261  no overlap, but family is a prefix of gene_name
    473 / 5,261  NEITHER - clone-style gene_name (AC020634.1, AL844851.3) and no rmsk overlap

The 473 break down as 229 SNORA, 92 SNORD, 54 YRNA, 35 RNU6, 32 SCARNA, 17 RNU1, 8 others.

For hg38 these came from a curated per-family genelists.* directory that no longer exists (see
the commented read_in_filelists call at parse_bowtie2_output_realtime_includemultifamily_SE.pl:43).
Mouse has no equivalent, so a rule must be DECIDED, and whatever is decided propagates into the
mouse index (which selects its Gencode portion by filelist membership) and into T-07.

Options:
 (a) Add a third source. Most of the residue is snoRNA box-class: SNORA = H/ACA, SNORD = C/D,
     SCARNA = scaRNA. Rfam family assignments (or snoDB) supply this and cover ~75% of the 473.
     YRNA/RNU6/RNU1 clone-named leftovers would still need something.
 (b) Fall back to the Gencode gene_type/transcript_type for anything unresolved, accepting that
     those rows carry 'snoRNA' rather than SNORA/SNORD. Cheap, but it reintroduces exactly the
     biotype-in-col4 defect T-09 exists to fix, just for 9% of rows.
 (c) Drop unresolvable rows from the filelist. They then also drop out of the index, changing
     which sequences reads can map to - measurable against the P-1 baseline, but a real change.

Recommend (a) with (b) as an explicit, logged fallback so the count of unresolved rows is visible
in the build rather than silent.

Note this is a HUMAN-side decision too: it determines whether an autogenerated hg38 filelist can
reproduce the reference closely enough for 475.22 (P-5).
notes:
RESOLVED 2026-08-11 with option (a) from the description: Rfam is the third source.

MECHANISM. Rfam names its families after the box class - SNORA70, SNORD56, SCARNA20 - which is
exactly the distinction the clone-named snoRNA rows are missing. New
bin/python/refdata_generation/build_rfam_family_table.py streams
  RNAcentral id_mapping/database_mappings/ensembl.tsv   transcript -> URS
  RNAcentral id_mapping/database_mappings/rfam.tsv      URS -> Rfam accession
  Rfam database_files/family.txt.gz                     accession -> Rfam ID
and maps the ID by prefix (SNORA*/SNORD*/SCARNA*/ACA* plus five exact names). Ships
refdata/hg38.rfam-family.tsv (1,449 rows) and refdata/mm.rfam-family.tsv (1,390). New
--rfam-family input is tier 4 of the Gencode family rule, after gene_name.

VALIDATION: on the 365 residue transcripts the 2020 reference labels, 255 predicted, 255 CORRECT,
ZERO WRONG. Not reference-derived, so unlike hg38.repbase-class-family.tsv it is not circular.

RESULT
  hg38  Gencode rows 4,859 -> 5,157; residue 857 -> 559; rows shared with the reference and
        identical on all five columns 4,633 -> 4,890
  mm10  Gencode rows 2,015 -> 3,090; residue 1,907 -> 833
  mm39  Gencode rows 1,994 -> 3,331; residue 1,928 -> 592
It matters far more for mouse: mouse gene symbols barely match the human RNU/SNORD patterns, so
tier 3 fires on only 22 rows and tier 4 carries 1,075/1,337.

INDEX IMPACT, the number this issue was really about: building the hg38 index from the generated
filelist now gives missing=112 (was 369), extra=267, MISMATCHING=0. Mouse indices rebuilt: mm10
4,413 -> 5,488 seqs, mm39 4,390 -> 5,727, both 100% covered by their filelist and inspect-clean.

AMBIGUITY HANDLED, NOT GUESSED: snoU2_19 and snoU2-30 (reference splits them SNORD/SCARNA) and
Vault (cannot choose VTRNA1/2/3) are listed AMBIGUOUS and predict nothing. SNORA73 (U17) also
splits 5 SNORA / 2 RNU105, but both RNU105 rows are gene_name RNU105C and settle at tier 3, so
Rfam is never consulted for them - tier order is what makes the validation the right comparison,
and there is a test pinning that.

REMAINING: 559 hg38 / 833 mm10 / 592 mm39 transcripts have no Rfam family at all. Nothing to hand
resolves them; --family-override is the escape hatch. Filing no follow-up - the tier that could be
built has been built.

title: hg38 index: 15 NR_ rRNA records missing; --custom-fasta undocumented
description:
The reference index contains 15 NR_-prefixed rRNA records (NR_145819.1-18S, NR_046235.3-28S, etc.). The generator has no source for them except --custom-fasta, which is undocumented and was not passed in the validation build, so the new index has zero.

These are not incidental: RNA45S/18S/28S/5-8S are the rRNA precursor families the pipeline special-cases (rRNA_extra_hash in parse_bowtie2_output_...pl), and RNA28S alone is the top-ranked element in the SE reference output at 5,399,580 reads. An index without them changes the single largest signal in the results.

Establish where the 15 records come from (RefSeq accessions suggest a curated FASTA) and make it an explicit input rather than an optional --custom-fasta.
acceptance_criteria: The 15 NR_ rRNA records are produced by an explicit, documented input; their source and accessions are recorded; the hg38 index contains all 15.
notes:
IMPLEMENTED + VERIFIED 2026-08-11. Closing.
--rrna-genbank (repeatable) replaces the undocumented --custom-fasta path; read_rrna_genbank() +
rrna_fasta(). All 15 NR_ records byte-exact against the reference. Tests in
tests/refdata_generation/test_trna_rrna.py. --custom-fasta remains for genuinely custom input.
Mouse does NOT inherit this rule -- NR_046233.2 carries no misc_feature; filed separately.

title: hg38 index: tRNA portion emits 631 entries, reference has 864
description:
Found while validating the T-05 rewrite. The tRNA portion is 233 entries UNDER the reference.

  reference 864 tRNA headers
  new build 631

read_trna() parses the UCSC/gtRNAdb tRNA track and dedupes; either the dedupe is too aggressive or the reference drew tRNAs from a second source. Note the reference index name contains 'wrepbaseandtRNA', and the MASTER_FILELIST has a separate tRNA column convention (T-07 rule 4 derives tRNA family by stripping the -N-M copy suffix), so the tRNA identity convention matters here too.
acceptance_criteria: The tRNA portion emits exactly 864 entries matching the reference; the source and dedupe rule are documented; a test covers it.
notes:
IMPLEMENTED + VERIFIED 2026-08-11. Closing.
--gtrnadb-fasta replaces --trna in generate_bowtie2_index.py; read_gtrnadb_fasta() + trna_fasta().
Full hg38 build validates 7606/7606 at --min-match 1.0 --max-missing 0 (was 0.99987).
Tests: tests/refdata_generation/test_trna_rrna.py.
Mouse gtRNAdb FASTAs downloaded and parsed cleanly by the same code (mm10 408, mm39 407 loci).

title: hg38 index: Gencode portion emits 5,708 transcripts, reference has 5,002
description:
Found while validating the T-05 rewrite. With the repeat and simple-repeat portions now exact, the Gencode portion is 706 transcripts OVER the reference.

  reference 5,002 ENST-style headers
  new build 5,708

The transcript-type filter (DEFAULT_TRANSCRIPT_TYPES in generate_bowtie2_index.py: snRNA, misc_RNA, snoRNA, rRNA_pseudogene, scaRNA, rRNA, Mt_tRNA, Mt_rRNA, vaultRNA) is commented 'verified against hg38 reference' but demonstrably admits too much. Either the type set is wrong, or there is a further filter the reference applied - note T-07 found the analogous Gencode selection there had to be restricted to MASTER_FILELIST minus specific rRNA/mito families, so a similar restriction may apply here.

Determine the rule by diffing the 706 extra transcript ids against the reference set and looking at what they have in common.
acceptance_criteria: The Gencode portion emits exactly 5,002 transcripts matching the reference id-for-id; the selection rule is documented with the evidence for it; a test covers it.
notes:
FIXED 2026-08-10. Rule derived from the reference, not guessed.

The transcript-TYPE filter could never have worked: the 706 over-selected transcripts span the SAME types as the reference (misc_RNA 455, snoRNA 179, snRNA 62, rRNA 9, rRNA_pseudogene 9, scaRNA 1), and the reference itself contains lncRNA (7), miRNA (1) and unprocessed_pseudogene (1) - types no plausible filter admits. The 'verified against hg38 reference' comment on DEFAULT_TRANSCRIPT_TYPES was wrong.

ACTUAL RULE: MASTER_FILELIST membership INTERSECT chromosome allowlist.
 - all 5,002 reference transcripts are in the MASTER_FILELIST, 0 exceptions
 - the 259 filelist ids the reference omits are ALL on GenBank scaffolds (GL000251.2, GL000255.2, KZ208915.1 ...); 0 are on chr*
 - the committed refdata/hg38.chrom-allowlist.txt (674 entries) reproduces 5,002 exactly

VERIFIED on a real build: 5,002/5,002 as an identical SET, and 5,001 of those also sequence-identical. The single sequence mismatch is ENST00000411342.6_PAR_Y, filed separately.

Implemented via --master-filelist and --chrom-allowlist; removed the orphaned --gtf, --transcript-types, DEFAULT_TRANSCRIPT_TYPES and read_gtf_transcript_types. Tests in tests/refdata_generation/test_gencode_selection.py.

DEPENDENCY NOTE: the index now depends on the MASTER_FILELIST, while T-09 has the filelist's REPEAT rows depending on T-05's provenance sidecar. That is a two-stage build (filelist Gencode rows -> index -> filelist repeat rows), not a cycle, but it inverts the T-05/T-09 dependency as recorded.

title: DECISION NEEDED: how are mouse repeat-family names assigned?
description:
T-05 investigation showed the repeat-family NAME cannot be recovered from the RepBase header alone, and hg38 only works because the reference index supplies ground truth. Mouse has no reference index, so the naming convention is a decision, not a derivation.

Evidence (all measured 2026-08-10 on real data):
 - RepBase header parsing tops out at ~93% (1143/1224 human, 1001/1079 mouse) and has structural traps: CR1_HS_CR1_Homo_sapiens needs right-to-left parsing, ALRa__SAT_Primates has an empty token
 - the assembly RepeatMasker track covers only 868/1224 = 71% of hg38 index names; 356 are RepBase satellite names (ALR, ALRA, ALINE) absent from the track
 - neither source alone, nor the obvious combination, reproduces the hg38 naming

Options:
 (a) Derive mouse names by RepBase header prefix with an explicit, committed rule plus a curated exception list for the residual ~7%. Reproducible and auditable, but the exception list is hand-made and unverifiable against any reference.
 (b) Restrict mouse repeat families to those present in the mm10/mm39 RepeatMasker track, accepting ~29% fewer families than the human set. Fully derivable, but changes what the pipeline can detect and makes mouse and human results not directly comparable.
 (c) Use the full RepBase header as the family name (no split). Unambiguous and fully derivable, but breaks name compatibility with the hg38 convention and with anything downstream that matches on family name.

This blocks T-05's mouse path, and by extension T-09, M-3, M-4 and every mouse artifact. It is an irreducibly curated item for the phase-4 analysis (475.20).
acceptance_criteria: A recorded decision with rationale; the chosen rule implemented in generate_bowtie2_index.py and validated to reproduce hg38 exactly; the mouse family-name set generated and spot-checked against known mouse repeat families (B1, B2, L1Md, IAP, MTA); the consequences for cross-species comparability written down.
notes:
DECIDED 2026-08-10: option (a). Outcome is better than the option described - the rule needs ZERO curated exceptions.

RULE (bin/python/refdata_generation/repbase.py):
  1. strip TAXON: trailing binomial (Genus_species per regex ^[A-Z][a-z]+_[a-z]+$) else the single trailing token

title: SE: pin tool versions; bowtie2 >=2.5 is the sole remaining CWL divergence
description:
With every SE output now compared against a fresh CWL 1.0.0 run, exactly ONE difference remains, and it is a tool-version artifact rather than a translation defect.

PROVEN CAUSE. Running both bowtie2 versions on the same fastq and index, same reads and same flags:
  bowtie2 2.2.6 (CWL module pin) : flag 256 secondary -> MAPQ 1
  bowtie2 2.5.5 (what >=2.5 resolved to) : flag 256 secondary -> MAPQ 255
Primary (flag 0) is MAPQ 1 in both; unmapped (flag 4) is 0 in both. bowtie2 changed to emit 255 ('unavailable', per SAM spec) for secondary alignments.

IMPACT IS COSMETIC, verified two ways:
 - blanking column 5 makes both rmDup.sam.gz and preRmDup.sam.gz byte-identical after sorting (17,691,900 lines each). Every read selection, position, flag, sequence, quality and optional tag matches exactly.
 - MAPQ is never read by any pipeline logic. The mapper keys on AS:i (map_repetitive_elements_se.py:73 get_as_score). The only tmp[4] uses in deduplicate.py (lines 95, 201) parse the gencode table-browser and a BED-like file, not SAM.

THE REPRODUCIBILITY PROBLEM IS BROADER THAN MAPQ. workflow/envs/dropin.yaml uses open-ended constraints, so the environment drifts every time it is rebuilt:
  declared            resolved on 2026-08-10
  python=3.10         3.10.20
  samtools>=1.17      1.23.1
  bowtie2>=2.5        2.5.5
  numpy               2.2.6
  pandas              2.3.3
  pysam               0.24.0
A rebuild in six months silently gets different versions. That, not the MAPQ value, is what stops the pipeline being reproducible.

DECISION REQUIRED: either (a) pin bowtie2==2.2.6 to reproduce the CWL SAM byte-for-byte, accepting an 11-year-old aligner, or (b) pin to the current exact versions and document MAPQ as a known, inconsequential divergence. Recommend (b): MAPQ is unused, and 2.5.5 is otherwise the better aligner. Either way every dependency needs an exact pin.
acceptance_criteria: Every dependency in workflow/envs/dropin.yaml carries an exact version pin; the chosen bowtie2 policy is recorded with its rationale; a rebuild of the env from scratch reproduces the same output; if option (b), the MAPQ divergence is documented where users will see it.
notes:
CLOSED 2026-08-10. Option (b) chosen: pin current versions, document MAPQ.

All six deps pinned exactly in workflow/envs/dropin.yaml. VERIFIED BY REBUILD, not by editing the spec: snakemake --conda-create-envs-only produced a fresh 599MB env (conda-env/edf4cca32e29858d00fd98de71668db1_) and all six installed versions match their pins (python 3.10.20, samtools 1.23.1, bowtie2 2.5.5, numpy 2.2.6, pandas 2.3.3, pysam 0.24.0). Small SE dataset re-run against the rebuilt env reproduces unchanged: RepFamilyReads 1784/0.80907 and 1162/0.55946, RNA28S 703.

MAPQ divergence documented in three places a user will hit it: workflow/envs/dropin.yaml (at the point of change, so editing a pin shows the consequence), CLAUDE.md Verification/Testing (with the warning that .sam.gz will NOT be byte-identical while every computed result is), and tests/cwl_baseline/README.md (with the awk incantation for masking column 5).

title: CWL->Snakemake: UsableReads fraction computed as usable/usable, always 1.0
description:
merge_parsed_files.py wrote the #READINFO UsableReads fraction as 'usable / usable', which is always exactly 1.0. The Perl original (merge_multiple_parsed_files.simplified_20191022.pl:45) divides by AllReads.

On the INV_B SE dataset:
  CWL 1.0.0 : #READINFO  UsableReads  17691900  0.783654640048363
  Snakemake : #READINFO  UsableReads  17691900  1.0

This is the 'what fraction of reads survived' QC metric, so the Python version silently reported a perfect 100% usable rate on every run ever made. GenomicReads and RepFamilyReads correctly divide by usable in both implementations; only this line was wrong.

It does not affect .nopipes.tsv/.withpipes.tsv, because calculate_fold_change_from_parsed_files.py derives enrichment from the TOTAL rows, which is why the output comparison passed while this was still broken. Found only by diffing the .parsed headers against a fresh CWL 1.0.0 run.

FIXED: divide by read_sums['all'], with a zero guard. Regression test added.
acceptance_criteria: UsableReads fraction equals usable/AllReads; a test asserts it is not 1.0 and matches the exact quotient; the .parsed header matches a CWL run to floating-point precision.
notes:
EVIDENCE CLARIFICATION 2026-08-10. The SE and PE evidence are NOT equivalent, and the closure summary blurred them.

SE - genuine comparison against the original:
  CWL 1.0.0 : #READINFO UsableReads 17691900 0.783654640048363
  ours      : #READINFO UsableReads 17691900 0.7836546400483626
  Field-to-field against a fresh CWL run; agrees to Perl's 15-significant-digit output precision. Artifact committed at tests/cwl_baseline/ecliprepmap-1.0.0-SE/INV_B.barcode1.parsed.readinfo.

PE - self-consistency ONLY, no original to compare against:
  There is no CWL PE .parsed anywhere in the repo. test-provenance/.../wf_ecliprepmap_pe/ holds only .nopipes.tsv and .withpipes.tsv, and those contain ZERO #READINFO lines (the fold-change script does not carry them through). No CWL PE baseline run was made - only the SE example was run.
  What was checked: the reported fraction equals usable/all from the same run's own counts (5637629/7249139 = 0.7776963581468089; 10621065/14167342 = 0.7496864972977995). That proves the formula is no longer hardcoded to 1.0, but it is the code agreeing with itself, not agreement with the Perl implementation.

The AC as written ('the .parsed header matches a CWL run') is satisfied by SE, so the closure stands. But PE's #READINFO fields have never been compared to an original, and that gap is now tracked separately.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA MET 2026-08-12 — PASS. Full numbers in
docs/CHANGELOG-refdata-validation-2026-07-25.md §10; comparison artifacts in
tests/p5_regenerated_hg38/.

All four hg38 artifacts regenerated from source by the committed generators; SE (70 jobs) and PE
(103 jobs) rerun on them; compared to the P-1 baseline. The baseline is sound: results/se_full and

ARTIFACT LEVEL: parsed_ucsc sorted-identical. MASTER_FILELIST recall .983 / precision .984. Index
7,494 shared headers with EVERY SHARED SEQUENCE BYTE-IDENTICAL (match_fraction 1.00000). BED
recall .999917 / precision .999913. No sequence differs anywhere; no Gencode transcript is

PIPELINE LEVEL:
  SE  total IP 17,505,462 -> 17,507,036 (+0.009%); 74/174 shared elements identical;
      23,629 reads moved (0.135%); 79 reads on dropped elements, 2,792 on new ones
  PE  total IP  5,590,588 ->  5,591,351 (+0.014%); 71/161 identical;
       8,645 reads moved (0.155%); 17 / 1,927

title: P-4: Gap analysis - what is auto-derivable vs what was manually curated
description: The central question for whether mouse can be generated at all. Known manual/curated residue that does NOT fall out of any source file: (1) the 12-entry DROP_EXACT list in refdata/repbase18.05-drop-exact.txt, derived by diffing against the hg38 reference index and unverifiable for mouse; (2) the gene_name->family map for MASTER_FILELIST col4 with its RNU/YRNA/RN7SL/SNORD special cases; (3) the chromosome allowlist pinned to an assembly release; (4) the GENCODE_EXCLUDED_FAMILIES set {RNA5S, RNA5-8S, MTTRNA, MTRNR1, MTRNR2}; (5) MASTER_FILELIST row order. Each is a place where hg38 could be reproduced by fitting to the answer, and where mouse has no answer to fit to. Classify every one as derivable-from-source, derivable-from-rule, or irreducibly-curated, and for the last category state how mouse gets a value and how that value is checked.
acceptance_criteria: Every curated constant enumerated with its derivation and its mouse counterpart or an explicit statement that none exists; each classified derivable vs curated; for each irreducibly-curated item, a stated mouse strategy and validation approach; the analysis flags any hg38 rule that was fit to the reference and therefore carries no evidence for mouse.
notes:
ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA MET 2026-08-13. Deliverable: docs/P4-curated-vs-derivable.md.

15 curated constants and shipped tables enumerated, each classified derivable-from-source /
derivable-from-rule / irreducibly-curated, each with its mouse counterpart or an explicit statement
that none exists, and each flagged for whether it was FIT TO THE HG38 ANSWER (reproduces hg38 by
construction and therefore carries no independent evidence).

9 of the 15 are fit-to-hg38 in whole or part. Eight have since been validated against mouse by an
independent check, given a mouse counterpart derived by rule rather than transferred, or shown
harmless:
  - repbase18.05-classes.txt (76 tokens, derived from the hg38 index): 0 unparsed on mouse, and
    unparsed is fatal, so a missing token could not pass silently
  - DROP_CLASSES/KEEP_PREFIX: the single hg38 exception MamSINE1_tRNA_ exists in the mouse library
  - chrom allowlists: mouse pinned to UCSC chrom.sizes; mm39's 61 names are exactly its rmsk
    scaffold set
  - index structural constants: 501 synthesized k-mers on all three assemblies
  - drop-exact and repbase-class-family: mouse has its own, derived by rule (475.11, 475.43)
  - gencode-family-order: fit to hg38 but between-family order changes no count (priority is keyed
    by family), so mouse inherits it harmlessly
  - GENE_NAME_FAMILY_RULES: was the worst hidden case -- 13 of 14 rules dead on mouse until -4ee

ONE IS NOT, and it is the finding this phase exists to produce. RMSK_AMBIGUOUS_REPNAMES =
{'U5','U17'} is the only curated constant measured to ACTIVELY DEGRADE the mouse artifacts, and it
does so silently (transcripts omitted, not mis-assigned, so nothing downstream complains):
    hg38  31 transcripts overlap rmsk 'U5' -> 31 resolved by gene_name, 0 dropped
    mm39  11 transcripts overlap rmsk 'U5' ->  1 resolved,              10 DROPPED
Human symbols encode the subfamily so the fallthrough always lands; mouse names them Gm*. The
justification does not exist in mouse, which has exactly one U5 family. Strategy and validation
recorded in the doc and in -9j2.

Two constants also flagged as having no source authority at all: REFERENCE_FAMILY_OVERLAP
{SNORD,YRNA}, which gates mouse and is by construction a statement about a human artifact's
blemish, and MIN_RMSK_FRACTION=0.99, which is INVENTED from three observations (caught the T-07
BEDs at 0.744 with huge margin, so nothing rests on the exact value).

description: test-provenance/ has the reference .nopipes.tsv/.withpipes.tsv for SE (INV_B.IP.umi.r1.fqTrTr.sorted.fq.barcode1) and PE (204_01_RBFOX2), but configs/, manifests/, scripts/ and reference-metadata/ are ALL EMPTY. generate_master_filelist.py writes the Gencode *biotype* into col4 where the reference has the curated repeat/gene FAMILY (misc_RNA/snRNA/snoRNA vs RNU6/YRNA/RN7SL/SNORD). Transcript-id overlap with the reference is only ~42% even after stripping version suffixes. The +/-1% line-count AC passed (26,252 vs 26,422 = 0.9936) while the content was substantially wrong.

Needs T-05's repeat family set + provenance sidecar. Blocks regeneration of mm10/mm39 UniqueGenomicElements, whose Gencode rule (T-07) requires a mouse MASTER_FILELIST.

Note: the T-07 Gencode partition (MASTER_FILELIST minus rRNA/mito families) and the T-05 §4b DROP_EXACT set describe the same partition and must stay consistent.

title: Mouse U5 rests on a single Gencode transcript; 116 snRNA transcripts are unresolved
description:
After 475.11 dropped the RepBase U5B1 record, mouse U5 snRNA is represented by exactly one transcript in each assembly (Rnu5g -> family RNU5G, ENSMUST00000093721.1 on mm10 and ENSMUST00000101817.3 on mm39, both present in the index). Human carries 34 across RNU5A-RNU5F. The decision follows the rule and human precedent and is not in doubt, but the thinness may be an annotation gap rather than biology: mm39 has 116 snRNA-biotype transcripts that resolve to no family at all (part of the 569-row small-RNA residue tracked by 475.41), all clone-named Gm*, and some are plausibly U5 copies. Mouse's residue is proportionally larger than human's - 569 of 3,929 candidate rows (14.5%) against hg38's 559 of 5,820 (9.6%).

M-9's smoke run is the cheapest probe: if mouse U5 reads pile up as unassigned or land on unique_* rather than RNU5G, the residue is the cause. Do not reinstate U5B1 to compensate - that reintroduces the double-count 475.11 removed; resolve the residue via --family-override instead.
notes:
CAUSE FOUND 2026-08-13 by P-4 (475.20). This is no longer speculative: the mouse U5 thinness is
one curated constant, and the missing transcripts are located exactly.

RMSK_AMBIGUOUS_REPNAMES = {'U5','U17'} in generate_master_filelist.py lists repNames that map to
more than one family, so tier 2 deliberately falls through to tier 3 (gene_name). That is free for
human and expensive for mouse:

                transcripts overlapping rmsk 'U5'   resolved by tier 3   dropped
    hg38                     31                          31                0
    mm39                     11                           1               10

Human symbols encode the subfamily (RNU5A-4P -> RNU5A, RNU5D-1 -> RNU5D), so the fallthrough always
lands. Mouse names the same genes Gm24043, Gm23102, Gm22365 ... so tier 3 returns nothing, the Rfam
tier has no U5 family, and 10 snRNA transcripts are dropped. They are 10 of mm39's 569 unresolved
small-RNA rows. U17 costs a further 4 the same way.

The justification for the fallthrough DOES NOT EXIST IN MOUSE: mouse has exactly one U5 family
(RNU5G), so 'U5' is not ambiguous there.

STRATEGY (unchanged conclusion, now with a mechanism): make the ambiguity assembly-aware instead of
global -- if an assembly's Gencode supplies exactly one family for an ambiguous repName, that
repName is not ambiguous for that assembly and tier 2 uses it. mm39 then maps all 11
U5-overlapping transcripts to RNU5G; hg38 is untouched, it genuinely has five U5 families.

VALIDATION: hg38 tier totals must not move (tier2 4,104 / tier3 755 / tier4 298), and mm39's
unresolved residue must fall by exactly the 10 U5 + 4 U17 transcripts, 569 -> 555.

Still do NOT reinstate the RepBase U5B1 record to compensate -- that reintroduces the double-count
475.11 removed. This is the right fix.

title: hg38 filelist: 354 RepBase satellite families have no rmsk class/family
description:
Found while landing T-09. 354 of the 1,224 RepBase families in the hg38 index have no genomic
instances in the modern UCSC rmsk track, so no repClass/repFamily is available for them and
generate_master_filelist.py falls back to the family name in all four annotation columns:

  new  ALR1 | ALR1 | ALR1 | ALR1 | ALR1
  ref  ALR1 | centr | centr | centr | Satellite

This is NOT cosmetic. col4 is the $type_label that read_in_filelists loads and print_output
counts with $count{$ensttype_join}++, so each of these 354 becomes its own counting family
instead of grouping under centr/Satellite/RTE. Reads on alpha-satellite variants would be
reported per-variant rather than pooled.

Mostly alpha-satellite (ALR*, ALRA, ALRB), other satellites, and a few LINE families (ALINE ->
RTE/LINE in the reference). Slash-qualified UCSC names are already handled -- ALR/Alpha resolves
ALR correctly -- these 354 are genuinely unannotated in hg38 rmsk.

The reference's values came from the RepeatMasker library of that era, which classifies library
entries whether or not they are annotated in a given assembly. We do not have it.

Options:
 (a) Dfam API lookup per family (dfam.org/api/families?name=ALR1) -- authoritative, but 354
     network calls and a new runtime dependency.
 (b) Ship refdata/repbase18.05-class-family.tsv derived from the RepeatMasker library if a copy
     can be found on TSCC.
 (c) Map the RepBase header CLASS token to a RepeatMasker class (SAT -> Satellite,
     Non-LTR_Retrotransposon -> LINE). Fixes col5 only; col4 -- the column that matters -- would
     still be the name, so this is the least useful option.
 (d) Accept and document.

Currently (d), logged with a count at build time. Related: -475.41 is the same shape of gap on
the Gencode side.
notes:
IMPLEMENTED 2026-08-11.

refdata/hg38.repbase-class-family.tsv: 1,224 curated family -> repFamily/repClass pairs lifted
from the RepBase block (lines 5277-6500) of the 2020 reference file. New optional
--repbase-class-family. resolve_repeat() now resolves in this order:
  1 curated small-RNA map  2 rmsk (incl. slash aliases)  3 curated table  4 name aliases
Aliases: NAME_I -> NAME_I-int (RepeatMasker's LTR internal-segment convention) and the species
tags _MM/_HS. Deliberately NOT _LTR/_DNA/_II/_MAM - those are class tokens inside the name.

RESULTS
hg38: RepBase block source = 867 rmsk + 354 curated + 3 small_rna, ZERO unresolved (was 354).
      Repeat rows identical to the reference: 1,265 -> 1,619 of 1,718. The remaining 99 are the
      post-2020 RepeatMasker reclassifications, left visible on purpose because rmsk outranks the
      curated table.
mm10: 674 rmsk + 215 curated + 27 rmsk_stem + 8 rmsk_int + 7 small_rna; unresolved 397 -> 147.
mm39: 713 rmsk + 181 curated + 27 rmsk_stem + 1 curated_stem + 7 small_rna; 358 -> 149.
      (mm39 needs no _int aliases - its newer rmsk already drops the -int suffix.)

VALIDATION of each alias before adding it:
  _MM stem: all 27 recovered families' stem-derived class agrees with their own RepBase class
            token (ERV1/ERV2/ERV3/LTR_Retrotransposon -> LTR, Satellite -> Satellite). 0 contra.
  _I-int:   8 mm10 families, all 8 consistent on the same check; validated on human ground truth
            too, though only 1 case is testable there (exact, 0 wrong).
  REJECTED longest-prefix inheritance: 18 of 161 matches wrong on hg38 (MER21/MER22/MER25 all
  match MER2). Not implemented.

REMAINING: 147/149 mouse families, of which only 9 have any mouse genomic footprint and all 9 are
now resolved by the _I-int alias. The rest have ZERO footprint, so they cost nothing today - but
B1, B1-DID and B2 are in the list, and those are the major mouse SINEs. They are unresolved
because UCSC names them B1_Mus1, B1_Mus2, B1F etc. and no bare 'B1' repName exists; a curated
mouse table (the mouse counterpart of the human one) is the way to close them, not another alias.
Tests: 11 added, 123 pass.

title: mouse rRNA: NR_046233.2 has no 18S/28S misc_feature annotation
description:
The hg38 rRNA rule (475.37) cuts 18S/28S from the misc_feature spans whose /note names them in
the RefSeq GenBank record. That rule does NOT transfer to mouse.

NR_046233.2 (Mus musculus 45S pre-ribosomal RNA, 13,400 bp) annotates only:
  source 1..13400, gene 1..13400, rRNA 1..13400
No misc_feature at all. read_rrna_genbank() therefore raises
"NR_046233.2: no misc_feature annotates ['18S', '28S']" -- correctly, rather than emitting a
truncated index.

So the mouse index can currently emit NR_046233.2-45S but not -18S/-28S. Options to evaluate:
 (a) use the standalone mouse rRNA RefSeq records (18S/28S/5.8S have their own accessions) and
     locate them within the 45S by exact substring match, mirroring what the human misc_features
     encode;
 (b) align the human subunit spans onto the mouse precursor;
 (c) accept 45S-only for mouse and document the divergence.
(a) is preferred: it is exact and verifiable the same way the human rule was.

Note the naming decision this implies -- the mapper's rRNA_extra_hash special-cases
RNA28S/RNA18S/RNA5-8S as members of RNA45S, so whatever mouse emits must key into MASTER_FILELIST
the same way.
notes:
IMPLEMENTED + VERIFIED 2026-08-11. Took option (a) from the description, generalized because a
strict substring match does not hold.

New --rrna-subunit LABEL=PATH (repeatable) supplies a standalone subunit RefSeq FASTA, used only
for subunits the precursor's GenBank record does not annotate. locate_subunit_by_anchors() finds
the span by the subunit's terminal 40-mers and requires each anchor to hit the precursor exactly
once; the emitted sequence is always the PRECURSOR's bases over that span.

Anchoring rather than substring matching is load-bearing:
  18S  NR_003278.3  1870 bp -> precursor 4008-5877, an exact copy
  5.8S NR_003280.2   157 bp -> precursor 6878-7034, exact (not emitted, matching human)
  28S  NR_003279.1  4730 bp -> precursor 8123-12849 = 4727 bp
The standalone Rn28s1 and the precursor's 28S are different rDNA copies and differ by a 3 bp
indel around position 4363 of the subunit; a substring match returns nothing at all.

Mouse invocation adds:
  --rrna-genbank examples/inputs/{mm10,mm39}/downloaded/rrna/NR_046233.2.gb
  --rrna-subunit 18S=.../NR_003278.3.fasta --rrna-subunit 28S=.../NR_003279.1.fasta
Inputs staged in both mm10 and mm39 downloaded/rrna/ (rRNA is not assembly-specific).

Human path is unchanged and still validates 7606/7606 at --min-match 1.0 --max-missing 0.
Tests: 8 added in tests/refdata_generation/test_trna_rrna.py, incl. the indel case, ambiguous
anchors, and the missing-fallback error. 83 pass.

title: hg38 index: ENST00000411342.6_PAR_Y sequence differs from reference
description:
With the Gencode selection fixed, 5,001 of 5,002 transcripts are sequence-identical to the reference index. The lone exception is ENST00000411342.6_PAR_Y.

PAR_Y transcripts are pseudoautosomal-region copies annotated on chrY that duplicate a chrX transcript. The likely cause is that parsed_ucsc_tableformat carries the chrX coordinates for the _PAR_Y id, so extraction pulls the chrX sequence, or the reference pulled from chrY while we pull from chrX (or vice versa).

Narrow but worth resolving: it is the only thing standing between the Gencode portion and a clean sequence-exact result, and PAR handling is the kind of edge case that silently transfers to mouse.
acceptance_criteria: The PAR_Y transcript's sequence matches the reference; the coordinate source for _PAR_ transcripts is documented; a test covers it.
notes:
FIXED 2026-08-11. Cause: hg38.fasta hard-masks the chrY PAR (analysis-set convention), so the
chrY extraction returned 120 Ns; the reference record is byte-identical to the chrX twin
ENST00000411342.6. remap_par_y_to_chrx() moves _PAR_Y ids on chrY to chrX before extraction. The
PAR is a literal duplicate across the two chromosomes, so this is correct on masked and unmasked
genomes alike. Test: test_gencode_selection.py::test_par_y_transcripts_are_read_from_chrx.

title: generate_bowtie2_index.py: --simplerepeats is required but never read

title: Perl mappers have the same unchecked-bowtie2-pipe defect as 475.16
description:
bin/perl/parse_bowtie2_output_realtime_includemultifamily_{SE,PE}.pl open bowtie2 as a read pipe (SE:77, PE:79) and never check the result:
  my $pid = open(BOWTIE, '-|', 'stdbuf -oL bowtie2 ... 2> $bowtie_out');
There is no '|| die' on the open and NO close(BOWTIE) anywhere in either script, so $? is never inspected. When bowtie2 fails to launch, while(<BOWTIE>) sees immediate EOF and the script exits 0 having written a 0-byte Rep.sam. This is the identical defect fixed in the Python mappers under 475.16, and it is what produced the original 0-byte Rep.sam that .forge/debug/causal-chain.json misdiagnosed as a transient fault in May 2026.

NOT FIXED DELIBERATELY, for three reasons:
1. The CWL uses 'baseCommand: [parse_bowtie2_output_realtime_includemultifamily_SE.pl]', resolved from PATH. Under 'module load ecliprepmap/1.0.0' that resolves to /tscc/projects/ps-yeolab4/software/ecliprepmap/1.0.0/bin/perl/, NOT this repo's copy - and the two files already differ. Patching the repo copy would not change what any CWL run executes.
2. These scripts are the reference implementation used to validate the Snakemake translation (tests/cwl_baseline/). Modifying them perturbs the baseline that equivalence testing depends on.
3. Fixing the installed module is a separate deployment action outside this repo.

Decide explicitly whether the CWL/Perl path is still supported. If it is, the fix belongs in the installed module and should be: close(BOWTIE) or die, then check $? and exit non-zero. If it is not supported, say so in CLAUDE.md and README, since both currently document it as an entry point.
acceptance_criteria: A decision recorded on whether the CWL/Perl path remains supported; if supported, the installed module's Perl checks the bowtie2 pipe exit status and the repo copy is resynced; if not, the docs stop presenting it as an entry point.

title: ecliprepmap 1.0.0 example is unrunnable as shipped on TSCC2
description:
Two independent breakages in /tscc/projects/ps-yeolab4/software/ecliprepmap/1.0.0/examples/repeat_mapping_SE.yaml:
1. All 'path:' entries use the pre-TSCC2 '/projects/...' prefix. /projects does not exist on TSCC2, so cwltool cannot stage any input.
2. The four INV_B input files under examples/inputs/ are broken symlinks into /projects/ps-yeolab4/software/eclip/0.7.0/... The targets exist under /tscc/projects/... but the links were never repointed after the TSCC1->TSCC2 migration.

Same likely applies to repeat_mapping_PE.yaml and to the 0.1.0 examples. Anyone following the README today gets a staging failure with no hint that the cause is a stale path prefix.
acceptance_criteria: Both example yamls run unmodified after the fix; symlinks repointed or replaced with real paths under /tscc/projects; PE example checked the same way; README notes the TSCC2 path convention.
notes:
THIRD breakage found 2026-08-10, and it is the one that actually stops the run: the SLURM/toil variant CANNOT use node-local scratch.

eCLIP_repelement_SE (non-singleNode) sets CWLRUNNER=slurm and distributes CWL steps as separate toil_job SLURM allocations. /scratch on TSCC2 is node-local NVMe (/dev/nvme0n1p1, 1.5T). Running with JOB_HOME on /scratch put toil's file store on one node's disk while SLURM scheduled the steps on other nodes, so the staged inputs were unreachable:

  parse_bowtie2_output_realtime_includemultifamily_SE.pl:464
    open(F,$fi) || die "no $fi\n"
  -> 'no <staged>/MASTER_FILELIST...wmiRs.list', exit 2, Max memory used 30MiB
  -> cwltool: Did not find output file with glob pattern ['INV_B.IP...Rep.sam']
  -> permanentFail

Confirmed by relaunching with JOB_HOME on /tscc/lustre/ddn/scratch/bay001 (1.7P, shared): the toil jobs then spread across tscc-4-18, tscc-11-57 and tscc-14-46 simultaneously and staging succeeded.

RULE: singleNode variants may use /scratch; the SLURM variants MUST use a shared filesystem (/tscc/lustre/ddn/scratch or /tscc/projects). Worth stating in the README next to the path fixes, since the failure surfaces as a misleading 'no <file>' from a Perl script rather than as a filesystem error.

title: M-9: End-to-end pipeline smoke run on mouse eCLIP data

title: Fix FASTA normalization and per-header hash validation
description:
## Problem
The sequence-validation AWK sketch replaces uppercase IUPAC symbols before uppercasing, so lowercase ambiguity codes such as rymk remain RYMK rather than NNNN. It also joins full sequences while describing the operation as a per-header hash comparison.

## Steps to Reproduce
Pipe a FASTA record containing lowercase rymk through the norm function in FIX-PLAN-bowtie2-index.md lines 90-93. The output sequence is RYMK instead of NNNN.

## Scope
Provide an executable, memory-conscious validator that canonicalizes FASTA records consistently and compares actual per-header digests.
acceptance_criteria: Normalization uppercases before converting all non-ACGT ambiguity codes required by policy to N; multiline and lowercase FASTA inputs are covered by tests; duplicate headers fail validation; per-header cryptographic hashes are compared; the validator reports shared, missing, extra, matching, and mismatching header counts and enforces the documented threshold.
close_reason: Replaced the broken AWK sketch with bin/python/refdata_generation/validate_fasta_equivalence.py: uppercases before mapping every non-ACGT byte to N (fixes lowercase rymk -> RYMK), per-header SHA-256 compared, duplicate headers exit 2, streams records so memory is O(headers). Reports new/reference/shared/missing/extra/matching/mismatching and enforces --min-match and --max-missing. 18 tests incl. multiline+lowercase FASTA, all IUPAC codes, MER5A same-header-different-sequence. Verified on the real 7,606-seq reference index.
